newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish automotive output rises 31 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Turkish automotive output rises 31 pct in Feb.

text.p: Turkey's motor vehicle output rose to 23,175 units in February, up 31 percent from February 1996, but down two percent to 44,221 units in the first two months of 1997, compared with the same 1996 period.
The automotive industry association (OSD) said car output jumped 25 percent to 14,999 in February, but fell 14 percent to 27,135 units in January-February, compared to a year ago.

Two-month output included 5,612 tractors, down 14 percent from the same 1996 period, 5,212 trucks, up 80 percent, 3,255 pick-ups, up 57 percent and 483 buses, up 46 percent, the OSD said in its monthly bulletin.
Car sales in February firmed to 28,488 units in January-February, up 9.3 percent from same 1996 period last year, mainly due to a sharp increase in imported car sales.

Domestic car sales dropped 11.8 percent to 19,960 units in January-February, while imported car sales surged to 8,528 from 3,442 in the same 1996 period. Domestic car sales had slumped to a five-year low of 6,159 in January.
Pick-up and minibus imports also leapt 90 percent to 3,847 in the first two months, compared to the same 1996 period.
The OSD said automotive industry exports fell 10 percent in the first two months of 1997, including tyres and other parts.
